Notes: Frank Ocean released “Thinkin Bout You” as the lead single of his debut studio album channel ORANGE on April 17, 2012. The single artwork features Raymond Buck, long-time friend of Frank Ocean, sitting at an arcade racing machine. This follows the nostalgic, video game-thematics of channel ORANGE. Buck performed additional vocals on the album’s opening track, “Start,” which features the startup chime of a Sony PlayStation. Buck later appeared in Ocean’s 2016 magazine Boys Don’t Cry, in a photoshoot titled “Crouching Tiger, Hidden Water Moccasin” on pages 240–253. Ocean also mentioned him in the first verse of “These Days,” a song intended for release on 7-inch vinyl in February 2020 that leaked online in May 2023.

The vinyl jacket contains monochromatic text & images that resemble the original project’s artwork, adorned with several new graphics etched into a silver-colored, reflective material under a layer of iridescent film.

Positioned on the right stands an impressive audio equipment rack, bearing a stern warning: “DON’T F***ING TOUCH!” This rack is a realm where audio engineers meticulously choreograph the harmonious interplay of signals from each microphone & instrument, utilizing the console’s intricate assortment of knobs & faders. Any unauthorized adjustments to this delicate equilibrium are almost certain to incite discord. The identifiable components on the stack include the Rane MP2 (Mixer Preamp), the Carvin EQ2015 (Equalizer), the Tascam 112 MKII (Cassette Recorder), and an array of other top-tier studio equipment.

Notes: The portrait of Frank Ocean is a detail of Wolfgang Tillmans, captured in Berlin, Germany, in 2015, and appears as the centerpiece of the primary artwork for Ocean’s studio album Blonde. The image is also used in one of three covers for Boys Don’t Cry magazine, released in companion with the album, and appeared in the magazine’s photographic series “I’m a Morning Person.” Tillmans later republished an unaltered version of the portrait in 2018 under the title “Frank, in the shower.”

Since the release of Blonde, all of Ocean’s music is published under the label, including his Apple Music 1 online radio show blonded RADIO.

Name: Blonde [V3]
Notes: The second alternate album artwork for Blonde is the only one of the three to spell the title as “blonde.” Frank Ocean shot the photo in Munich, Germany, circa 2015. It features a man hotboxing in a car, smoking what looks like a joint of marijuana. The image appears on pages 40–41 of Boys Don’t Cry magazine, in a series titled “Glitterboy Down (Best Day Ever).” Ocean later used the photo in the artwork for blonded RADIO, his intermittent Apple Music 1 online radio show, launched in 2017. Other cover art for this album features the word “blond” even though the album is listed as “Blonde” on Apple Music, Spotify, and other music outlets. Additionally, Ocean has referred to the album as both Blond & Blonde on multiple occasions, only adding confusion. The use of two interchangeable spellings certainly seems intentional, and likely centers around Ocean’s bisexuality. People mentioned in the album could be male or female or alien.

The front cover features a monochromatic version of Blonde’s primary artwork, the design of Michel Egger & Thomas Mastorakos with photography by Wolfgang Tillmans.

Name: Blonde Black Friday Vinyl
Notes: The back cover of the 2016 Black Friday LP release of Frank Ocean’s Blonde is the design of Michel Egger & Thomas Mastorakos. The tracks are arranged in four corners as they appear on each side of the accompanying vinyl. The cover lists the song “Night.s” with an alternative spelling to its streaming release. The photograph in the center by Viviane Sassen features Ocean wearing a custom Arai GP-6RC helmet and a hoodie with a reversed NASCAR logo, standing on a racetrack in Tokyo, Japan. The image also appears on page 165 of Boys Don’t Cry magazine, in a series titled “Foxface,” and as one of the three magazine covers, known to fans as the ‘helmet cover.’

Name: Nikes [Single]
Notes: At some point before the release of Blonde in August 2016, Frank Ocean commissioned London-based type designer Kia Tasbihgou to create artwork for a series of singles, including the songs “Nikes,” “White Ferrari,” “Ivy,” “Nights,” “Self Control,” and “Both Sides” (likely an early name for “Chanel,” released in March 2017, after the release of Blonde). The covers include a catalog number in the top-right corner with the suffix “BDC” (or Boys Don’t Cry, an early name of what became Blonde and the title of Ocean’s magazine, released in companion with the album). Ultimately, “Nikes” was the album’s only single, released as a music video (without Tasbihgou’s artwork). Tasbihgou shared the unused covers on Instagram in March 2017.

Era: Look At Us, We're In Love
Name: In My Room [V1]
Notes: The cover artwork for the streaming release of “In My Room” was designed by Michel Egger, with photography by Ian Kenneth Bird and PrEP+ styled graphic lettering by Nejc Prah. The cover features the same photograph of Frank Ocean used as the artwork for episode 009 of blonded RADIO that premiered the song on November 3, 2019. Ocean’s posture in the image resembles one of the seventeen silhouettes lining the bottom of the artwork. The cover resembles the artwork of the October 2019 single “DHL,” which featured a similar layout, and the April 2020 digital singles “Cayendo” & “Dear April,” which featured one of the many silhouettes. Unlike the artwork released with the other 7-inch vinyl singles, the streaming version of “In My Room” did not use the vinyl’s center label as its cover.

Name: Blonde [Vinyl Re-Press]
Notes: On December 17, 2022, blonded reissued Frank Ocean’s Blonde on vinyl. The release included a redesigned gatefold, a 12" × 36" lyrics foldout, and a 12" × 24" poster. The LP sold on blonded.co for $65 and began shipping in January 2023. The refreshed cover artwork adds an “e” to the album’s title and removes the barcode beneath the photo. The gatefold is printed in full color on a bright white canvas, unlike the original Black Friday LP.

Name: Channel Orange [Vinyl Re-Press]
Notes: The front cover of the 2025 channel ORANGE gatefold vinyl includes a redesigned album artwork featuring a three-by-four photo collage of scenes from Frank Ocean’s 2012–2013 television appearances, promoting his debut studio album. The cover is inspired by the concept of channel surfing through memories, as explored on channel ORANGE. It iterates the “Smiling on TV” digital banner & poster released by blonded on the album’s decennial anniversary, July 10, 2022.

Name: Channel Orange [Vinyl Re-Press]
Notes: The back cover of the 2025 channel ORANGE gatefold jacket also features a three-by-four photo collage, concluding the sequence of scenes from Frank Ocean’s 2012–2013 television appearances, channel surfing through his memories. The back cover does not list the album’s title, tracks, or publishing information, in favor of a minimalist design. The gatefold is packaged in disposable plastic wrap with a barcode sticker on the back cover that reads, “810126907417.”
